clue.text: The bit left over is no longer available-was divided

parts.note: a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu
cut is a past tense meaning was divided or split

explanation.surface: A remnant is described as unavailable, having already been split up.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is a scrap of timber, cloth or paper remaining after the main piece has been taken.

clue.text: A number — about fifty—— produce ingredients for cakes

definitions.note: plural phrase defining a singular mass noun: the substance used in baking

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the number wraps round the other letter

parts.note: four is a number
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Some quantity, roughly fifty, yields what goes into a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground wheat is the basic dry ingredient of most cakes and bakes.

clue.text: Might placate or annoy her — she got the needle!

indicators.note: to annoy is to disturb, so the letters of the two words are stirred up

explanation.surface: A woman who might be soothed or irritated is said to have been given an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got the needle' looks like being annoyed or injected; it points to Cleopatra's Needle, the Egyptian obelisk on London's Thames Embankment named after the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient obelisk on London's Embankment is known by the Egyptian queen's name, so she 'got' it.

clue.text: Disturb siesta and get a cup of tea

indicators.note: disturbing a nap jumbles it, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Interrupt someone's afternoon nap and have some tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A tassie is a Scots word for a small cup, used in crosswords more than in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Tassie is Scottish dialect for a small drinking cup.

clue.text: Against trying to persuade someone to disregard the rules of the court

definitions.text: disregard the rules of the court
definitions.note: verb phrase defining the noun: the offence of ignoring a court's authority

parts.note: con is the opposite of pro, meaning against
to tempt is to try to persuade someone to do something unwise

explanation.surface: Someone opposes coaxing another person into flouting legal procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is the offence of disobeying or showing disrespect for a court's orders.

clue.text: One who hits back might be a shoplifter

definitions.meaning: a person who retaliates in a fight or launches a reply to an assault
read as two words, someone attacking a shop counter, raiding the till or goods

explanation.definitionFit: A retaliating fighter makes a counterstrike; split, the phrase also means a thief who raids a shop counter.

clue.text: Perhaps 5 reserve on written record

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Perhaps 5 reserve on written record': NOTE + BOOK works, but the definition 'Perhaps 5' fits neither 5-across CONTEMPT nor 5-down COUNTERATTACKER, so the cross-reference is wrong as held.

clue.text: Among them Bert found something red hot

indicators.note: among signals the letters lie within the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man called Bert discovered something burning among a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing coal or fragment left in a dying fire is still red hot.

clue.text: Long drink included very soft fruit

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

indicators.note: included means the drink holds the musical marking inside it

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A tall drink came with some very soft fruit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long drink' looks like one phrase; 'Long' is a verb meaning pine, and 'very soft' is the music direction pianissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical fruit with spiky skin and sweet yellow flesh.

clue.text: Sounds like a fair weather sailor-but may get turned over

definitions.note: past participle defining a noun: a leap in which the body flips heels over head

indicators.note: the clue openly says the phrase that follows is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a sailor who only goes out in summer could be called a summer salt, salt meaning seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor who only goes out in good weather might still capsize.
explanation.walkthrough: An old salt is a seasoned sailor, so one who sails only in fine weather is a 'summer salt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A somersault is an acrobatic roll in which the body flips head over heels.

clue.text: Riverside where deposits may accumulate

definitions.meaning: the sloping ground beside a river
a financial institution where savings are paid in and build up

explanation.definitionFit: A river has sloping edges of that name, and a financial institution holding savings has the same name.

clue.text: He keeps mum in order

parts.note: mum means silent, and order is a religious community: a monk vowed to silence in a monastic order

explanation.definitionFit: Monks of this Cistercian order are known for their strict observance of silence.

clue.text: Exclude a chap from a job at 24!

definitions.note: 24 is the answer to 24-down, a pub; the definition names the worker who holds that job

parts.note: to bar someone is to exclude them
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man is banned from working at the nearby pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 24-down is LOCAL, the nearby pub, so the job there is serving drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's local staff includes the man who pulls pints behind the counter.

clue.text: Don't eat quickly

definitions.meaning: to go without food, as at Lent or Ramadan

explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from food is to go without; the same word is an adverb meaning rapidly.

clue.text: A car was driven backwards by one hand somehow, because of the spiders

indicators.note: a car driven backwards is reversed, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some unstated order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A car reversed by someone using just one hand, all on account of some spiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was driven backwards' turns CAR into RAC; 'somehow' shuffles I and HAND into HNIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Arachnida is the zoological class containing spiders, scorpions and mites.

clue.text: These might form the roost of quiet group

definitions.text: These might form the roost of quiet group

indicators.note: to group things is to arrange them, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Birds might gather on these as a perch for a peaceful flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' rearranges ROOST, OF and P; the whole clue also describes where birds settle.
explanation.definitionFit: The tops of houses are a common perch where pigeons and starlings settle for the night.

clue.text: Musician who organises his own publicity

definitions.meaning: a player of a brass instrument
someone who blows his own trumpet, boasting about himself

explanation.definitionFit: A brass player is named after his instrument; a self-promoter blows his own horn, so to speak.

clue.text: Report containing useful ammunition

parts.note: a news report, read as a round of ammunition with the word in after it, a gun's report

explanation.definitionFit: A news bulletin is a short official report, and split it reads as a round loaded in.

clue.text: Weed killer some spread around water

indicators.note: spread around says one piece is laid round the outside of the other

parts.note: some of something is part of it
aqua is Latin for water

explanation.surface: A gardener sprays some weedkiller around the pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraquat is a powerful herbicide used to destroy unwanted plants.

clue.text: Employer's not sure

definitions.note: read as employer is: the definition is a person who employs something

indicators.note: not sure suggests the word is unsettled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses a thing is its employer in the sense of putting it to use.

clue.text: Hesitation as the queen takes the rubber

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: After some hesitation, the queen picks up the eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber is the British word for a block that removes pencil marks.

clue.text: A time in great slavery

indicators.note: in places the short time unit inside the word for great

parts.note: great can mean tall in size
hr is an abbreviation for hour, a time

explanation.surface: There was a long period of terrible servitude.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in thrall is to be in bondage or servitude.

clue.text: Dithering maid takes time to let someone in

indicators.note: a dithering person is in a state of confusion, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An indecisive maid takes ages to open the door to a visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit is to allow entry to a visitor.

clue.text: Bad start in paultry affair broken off unexpectedly

indicators.note: in puts the first letter inside the rearranged word
an affair broken off is shattered, so the letters of the word are scrambled
start points to the first letter of the word bad

explanation.surface: A rotten beginning to a trivial romance that ended suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paultry' is printed that way, a play on poultry; 'affair broken off' scrambles it to ARUPTLY, and 'in' puts B, the start of 'Bad', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without warning happens suddenly, and so abruptly.

clue.text: Nearby hostelry

definitions.meaning: close at hand, in the neighbourhood
a pub, specifically the one closest to home that someone regularly visits

explanation.definitionFit: Something in the neighbourhood is close at hand; in Britain the same word means a regular nearby pub.

clue.text: Solid business

explanation.definitionFit: Something solid is hard and unyielding; a business is also called a company of that name.

clue.text: A thief or a shop assistant does this

definitions.text: A thief or a shop assistant does this

parts.words: A thief or a shop assistant does this
parts.note: a thief steals the goods, while a shop worker counts the inventory: both deal with merchandise in different senses

explanation.definitionFit: Stocktaking is counting a shop's inventory; a thief helps himself to the goods, in another sense.

clue.text: It fixes up naughty Rene after 13

indicators.note: after places the rearranged name behind the word from 13-across

parts.note: 13-across is the word meaning go without food or quickly

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters of the name are disordered

explanation.surface: Something that fastens follows a misbehaving woman named Rene.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp, buckle or button holds things together, so it fixes them.

clue.text: Not often right about unreliable layer

indicators.note: unreliable means the letters of the word cannot be trusted to stay in order

explanation.surface: The right hen is rarely seen to lay dependably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' just links the pieces; 'unreliable' shuffles LAYER into ARELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens seldom occurs infrequently.
